final.memo:
We have carefully reviewed the business and decided to pass. Our investment standard requires simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative businesses with dominant market positions and durable long-term growth [D01]. The Company currently fails to meet these criteria, as its financial results are plagued by recurring GAAP losses and an inability to fund capital expenditures and dividends from operating cash flow [D02], [D03].

Unlike the high-quality compounders we target in our Pershing Square 3.0 era, this business is structurally tethered to volatile global commodity cycles [D01], [D04]. This reliance on extrinsic factors we cannot control introduces a level of risk and unpredictability that is incompatible with our portfolio mandate [D01], [D04].

The market’s focus on the stock's 55.4% drawdown and its recent removal from the Dow Jones Industrial Average misses the underlying issue: the lack of a reliable earnings path [D03], [D04]. Because the business requires external financing to sustain its capital-intensive operations and dividend policy, the valuation remains disconnected from any meaningful fundamental floor [D02], [D03].

We pass on the opportunity to invest, as there is no catalyst or management-led shift that can bridge the gap between the current cash-burning reality and our required 20% rate of return. We will continue to focus our capital on businesses that demonstrate consistent, capital-light growth rather than those subject to the boom-and-bust cycles of the energy sector [D01], [D02].
